title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter & token/event ordering in streaming chunking/framing
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming framing that could emit delimiter events out of order with partial JSON/token events, which caused JSON parsers and OpenAI-compatible clients to observe truncated/invalid JSON in streaming responses. No API contract changes.
description:
Context: Several customers and internal e2e runs surfaced flaky failures when consuming SSE streaming responses containing partial JSON payloads (structured output / tool calling flows). Root cause: under high concurrency/continuous-batching the streaming runtime could emit delimiter events ("[DELIM]") that signal object/field boundaries before some token-level events were flushed, leading to out-of-order token/event interleaving. This manifested as truncated or malformed JSON on the client side and caused the OpenAI compatibility layer to mis-interpret structured outputs.

What this PR does: fixes framing and ordering in the SSE streaming path across the runtime and OpenAI compatibility adapter. Key points: 1) Ensure a single ordered writer path for token events and delimiter markers so relative ordering is deterministic even under concurrency. 2) Serialize partial-JSON tokens using the new framing API that batches delimiter emission with the last token for a given JSON fragment. 3) Add regression & fuzz tests that reproduce previously-observed races and assert client-observed ordering invariants. 4) Update the OpenAI-compat stream adapter to respect the new framing markers and to delay final delimiter emission until underlying token writes confirm flush.

Checklist:
- [x] Root cause analysis and reproducer test added
- [x] Fix implemented in runtime (C++/Rust) and surfaced to Go adapter
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Fuzz tests for partial JSON framing
- [x] Docs updated (streaming behavior and compat notes)

Notes: The change keeps the external API unchanged; it only affects ordering guarantees for streaming payloads (making them stronger). This resolves multiple flaky failures in the OpenAI compatibility test suite and a recent SRE incident (SUP-1189). Related Linear: ENG-3421, ENG-3422.

How to review: focus on runtime/sse/framing.py for the ordering primitive, serializer.cc for the flush semantics, and api/openai_compat/stream_adapter.go for adapter changes. Tests live under tests/sse/ and reproduce the race condition via a deterministic scheduler harness.

Backwards compatibility: no behavior changes for non-JSON streams. For structured/partial JSON streams, clients will now observe consistent delimiter/token ordering (fixes flakiness).
